hook: Replaced a daily manual calibration analysis with an unattended pipeline that reports before the shift starts.

problem.statementExec: Every morning began with hours of hand-built statistics. New production batches had to be validated against a reference batch across 18 tolerance parameters — and a drifting batch only got caught if someone found the time to look.
problem.statementTech: Each morning, engineers manually pulled multi-database test data, applied filters, ran an 18-parameter tolerance comparison of new production batches against the reference batch, and compiled reports by hand. Results depended entirely on who was on duty, batch switches required config edits and a redeploy, and alerts depended on someone noticing the data.
painPoints: Hours of expert engineering time consumed every single day
A batch switch meant config files, scripts and a redeployment
Alerts fired only when a human happened to notice
marginNotes: 30 days of history · tens of millions of rows

approach.summaryExec: We replaced the entire manual workflow with three connected parts: a web dashboard that runs the process, an unattended daily pipeline that does the analysis, and a watchdog that guarantees the analysis itself is healthy.

stages.label: Configure
stages.captionExec: Engineers add or retire batch pairs in a 30-second web form — no code, no config files, no redeploy.
stages.captionTech: Batch assignments persist in a managed relational store; the next scheduled run picks them up automatically.

stages.label: Pull
stages.captionExec: Every morning the pipeline gathers 30 days of production test data on its own.
stages.captionTech: Parallel-chunked queries against the production data warehouse handle tens of millions of records.

stages.label: Sufficiency gate
stages.captionExec: If not enough new data has arrived, yesterday's result carries forward instead of a shaky new one.
stages.captionTech: Below the new-sample threshold the run is skipped and the prior result is re-recorded, keeping every day statistically meaningful.

stages.label: Analyse
stages.captionExec: Two views every day: the full cumulative comparison, and a 24-hour early-warning window — across all 18 parameters.
stages.captionTech: Cumulative (full batch history vs reference) and daily (last 24h) windows evaluated against per-parameter tolerances, with two alert scenarios: simultaneous breach, and 3 consecutive daily breaches.

stages.label: Alert
stages.captionExec: The moment a threshold is breached, the owning team gets a notification with the proposed calibration values.
stages.captionTech: Team-messaging webhooks carry batch names, violating parameters and proposed calibration values — no one has to check anything.

stages.label: Watchdog
stages.captionExec: A second automated job checks the first one every morning, so a silent failure can never hide.
stages.captionTech: Post-run health monitor verifies execution, stored results and logs; failures raise an immediate alert before the business day is lost.

parts.role: control centre · batch management & results viewer

engine.evaluation: Deployed on the production site and run daily across multiple concurrent batch pairs. During rollout, engineers shadowed the automated results against manual calculations until the numbers matched; the health monitor and full run history keep every result auditable after the fact.

value.before: Hours of expert work each morning, results scattered in spreadsheets and emails, batch switches requiring developer involvement, and failures surfacing only when someone looked.
value.after: A single dashboard, an unattended pipeline with results ready before the shift starts, 30-second batch switches, and instant alerts the moment any parameter drifts out of tolerance.
